data.title: US Army Reserve seeks feedback on potential readiness for action in Cuba: CBS
data.description:
• The US Army Reserve is asking for information from subordinate commands on the availability of units that could be made available to US Southern Command, according to a document obtained by CBS News.
  • Although Cuba is not mentioned anywhere in the document, several US officials told the news network that the information is for military planning regarding Cuba.
  • The message states that units would "possibly [be] needed in 90-120 days," and responses were due back by Sept. 25.
  • Units mentioned in the request include a combat sustainment support battalion; an engineer battalion; and an expeditionary sustainment command to oversee logistics.
  • The Army Reserve did not respond to CBS News. Southern Command said that it does "not disclose details or comment on U.S. operational movements or potential deployment timelines associated with current or future operations, contingencies, or planning."
  • President Trump told reporters at the White House Saturday that he doesn't believe military action in Cuba will be necessary as the two countries want a deal.
  • "Cuba is failing very badly," the president said. "We want to help Cuba. We want to open Cuba up to our people."

data.title: TikTok in $100M+ settlement with Alabama
data.description:
• Alabama will receive at least $100M from TikTok (TIKTOK) as part of a settlement that accused the online video platform of having addictive features and exposing young people to "serious mental harms."
  • The state is eligible for up to $300M if other conditions are met.
  • Terms call for TikTok to implement a two-hour daily time limit for children that use the platform; restricting access from 12a to 6a; stronger content moderation provisions; and stronger parental controls. 
  • The settlement, the first of its kind in the US, comes as Alabama's case against TikTok was set to go to trial on Sept. 28.

data.title: SA Asks: Is now the time to buy streaming stocks? If so, which ones?
data.description:
Many of the major streaming stocks have lost significant ground since January, with Paramount Skydance (PSKY), Netflix (NFLX), Versant (VSNT), and Comcast (CMCSA) down over 20% year-to-date.

We asked Seeking Alpha analysts Florian Muller and Daniel Jones if now was the time to buy streaming stocks and, if so, which ones?

Florian Muller: Investors' enthusiasm around streaming is clearly past its peak, and rightfully so. They have recognized that streaming is not a new growth story but a simple shift in the type of TV consumption and the technology that delivers it. 

For legacy media companies like Disney (DIS) and Comcast (CMCSA), this renders streaming a necessary new income stream, offsetting linear TV declines. For pure players like Netflix (NFLX) or Amazon's (AMZN) Prime Video, it created an opportunity to capture shares in the broader entertainment realm. Streaming has reached a rather saturated steady state, where growth is harder to come by and competition is fierce.

After skepticism around Netflix (NFLX) a year ago, I am turning more bullish now that the stock trades 33% lower. These valuation levels around 20x earnings more realistically represent the maturing state and slowing growth of the industry. 

I have long had an even more bullish stance on Disney (DIS) and Comcast (CMCSA). Neither, however, are to be seen as streaming stocks. Real-life experiences are far more profitable ways of monetizing their IP, and both companies have announced new theme parks for the early 2030s.

Daniel Jones: Even though it is not a pure play in the streaming space, my favorite streaming company has got to be The Walt Disney Company (DIS).

One of the reasons why I like Disney (DIS) from a streaming perspective is because of its diversification. You're not buying into a single streaming platform. You're buying into three of them: Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN. And all of them are significant in size and varied in terms of content. Plus, management continues to make major investments and see meaningful traction when it comes to these platforms. 

Management has spoken of its efforts to connect Disney's services into a single ecosystem, and this specifically involves Disney+. For instance, the company hopes to turn it into a comprehensive membership ecosystem that integrates high-value, always-on benefits with its storytelling. Recently, the company allowed Hulu Standalone and Bundle subscribers to link profiles, watch history, and manage subscriptions on Disney+, and even added social clips to Disney+ Verts. 

Disney also entered into a major deal with TikTok that will bring creators to the forefront of the platform by using a curated feed of fan-created content featuring its characters and stories. As for ESPN, the company has unlocked a selection of content on Disney+ domestically. That started in 2024 but has been expanding globally. 

This all tells a story of a business that is integrating assets in a way that creates a flywheel effect while facilitating product stickiness that makes customer churn less likely over the long run. This is a phenomenal strategy if you ask me and something that other streaming platforms largely lack. 

The benefit to investing in Disney (DIS) as a streaming play is that you get more than just streaming. And the business as a whole seems to be doing quite nicely. For the first nine months of 2026, revenue ended up being 6.2% higher than the year before. And while net income was down due to changes in taxes, adjusted operating cash flow ended up rising 6.7%. So clearly, the company is doing well at the moment.

(Daniel Jones runs the investment newsletter Crude Value Insights.)

data.title: Real estate stocks slump amid rising bond yields, sector rotation into technology
data.description:
Wall Street's major market averages advanced during the week ended September 25 while Treasury yields surged, oil and gas markets remained in focus, and President Xi Jinping and President Trump wrapped up their summit.

However, rising bond yields and a sector rotation into technology stocks led to a decline in real estate stocks in general.

Mortgage rates jumped this week, crossing the 7% threshold on average by Thursday. 30-year fixed-rate mortgages hit 7.49% on Friday amid the bond selloff, the highest in two and a half years, CNBC News reported.

KB Home (KBH) stock saw a reversal in gains despite posting a Q3 earnings beat. The stock price decline was driven by a lowering of margin guidance at the homebuilder's earnings conference call on the back of a rough housing market.

On the difficult backdrop, the S&P 500 Real Estate Index Sector (SP500-60) decreased 1.36% week-over-week to 266.46 points, while the accompanying State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLRE) was down 2.28% to $41.56.

The Dow Jones REIT Indx Equity REIT Total Return Index declined 1.15%, while the FTSE Nareit All Equity REITs index retreated 1.18%.

Weekly Winners & Losers

Among largecap stocks, telecom tower REITs Crown Castle (CCI) (-7.14% W/W to $67.84) and SBA Communications (SBAC) (-6.97% W/W to $166.15) led the losers.

Telecom tower REITs were recently slapped with bearish outlooks by investment banks on broader sector underperformance.

Meanwhile, Host Hotels & Resorts (HST) led the gainers, adding 2.66% from the prior week to $22.42.

Welltower (WELL) followed with a 1.09% gain to $231.37. The week saw J.P. Morgan raise its recommendation on the stock to Overweight from Neutral, citing WELL trades at one of the lowest implied cap rates. 

For midcap gainers, Howard Hughes (HHH) (+13.63% W/W to $68.43) led the pack.

Next week, Howard Hughes is set to host its annual shareholders meeting, which will include discussions on plans to accelerate transformation into a diversified holding company, including efforts to significantly reduce the capital intensity of Howard Hughes Communities, the company's real estate subsidiary, and increase capital available for investment in Vantage, the company's insurance subsidiary.

Medical Properties Trust (MPT) extended gains from the prior week, when it sold Idaho Falls Community Hospital and Mountain View Hospital for $413M. The stock closed 5.00% higher at $3.57.

Fermi (FRMI) topped the losers in a week that saw the REIT and TensorWave amend their data center lease and services agreement to extend the closing date under the lease by a month.

Additionally, Fermi signed a management agreement with CBRE Group (CBRE) to run and maintain building one, its first data center in the Texas Panhandle.

The stock fell 9.24% from the previous week to $4.52.

Compass (COMP) followed with a 6.94% decline to $9.38.

Among smallcap stocks, Adamas Trust (ADAM) (-8.64% W/W to $8.14), TPG RE Finance Trust (TRTX) (-8.64% W/W to $6.56), Transcontinental Realty Investors (TCI) (+6.35% W/W to $42.88), and Empire State Realty Trust (ESRT) (+4.58% W/W to $4.11) were the notable movers.

Here is a look at subsector performances for the week:

data.title: CNN barred from travelling with Trump on Air Force One on Saturday
data.description:
• CNN, which is owned by Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), said that the White House informed the network its staff would not be allowed on Air Force One on Saturday as the president flies to Knoxville, Tenn., for a college football game between Tennessee and Texas.
  • The network was selected to cover the travel as part of its role in the White House press pool until the Trump administration told CNN on Friday night it would be barred.
  • No other news outlet was named to take CNN's place, so there will be no television news coverage of the Tennessee trip.
  • The decision comes after the administration initially defied an order given by a federal judge on Sept. 24 mandating that reporters from CNN, MS Now (VSNT), and Politico have their White House credentials restored. They were allowed back on the grounds later in the day.   
  • Dear readers: We recognize that politics often intersects with the financial news of the day, so we invite you to click here to join the separate political discussion.

data.title: Trump, Xi agree to cut tariffs on $30B worth of goods
data.description:
• The White House late Friday said that President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping had agreed to reduce tariffs on $30 billion worth of non-sensitive goods traded in each direction.

  • US exports covered by the agreement include agricultural products, fish and seafood, wood products, cosmetics, and medical devices. US imports from China include consumer products such as small appliances, toys, holiday decorations, and children’s car seats.

  • China has also agreed to import at least 10 million metric tons of coal from the US in 2027 and 2028, according to a White House fact sheet.
  • Both countries also formed a Board of Investment whose mission is "to discuss potential investment opportunities and investment-related impediments and to provide a structured channel for the two sides to address commercially meaningful investment-related issues."
  • The Trump administration also said that the two nations would address concerns on supply chain shortages of rare earth minerals "with the goal of ensuring shipment levels return to appropriate levels."

data.title: Trump rejects Iran ceasefire, plans to resume bombing after midterms: WSJ
data.description:
• President Trump has reportedly turned down an Iranian proposal for a 7-day ceasefire and has told advisors that he plans to restart bombing Iran after the midterms on Nov. 3.
  • The president is apparently skeptical of Iran's ability to meet his demands, The Wall Street Journal reported.
  • Iran's proposal would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart nuclear discussions. In exchange, the U.S. would end its blockade of Iranian ports, according to the newspaper.
  • The extent of potential future attacks is unknown. Officials told the Journal that the president is reluctant to resume major combat operations, in part because of declining supplies of munitions.

data.title: Financials slump amid sector rotation into technology; Wells Fargo, Morgan Stanley in week's losers
data.description:
Wall Street's major market averages advanced as continued AI spending drove capital markets activity and sector rotation into technology.

A surge in AI-related capital expenditure by major firms is reshaping technology capital markets, driving record levels of capital-raising activity, according to a report by S&P Global Market Intelligence.

This is creating unprecedented demand for financing, while simultaneously driving sector rotation as investors seek exposure to the AI supply chain, the report noted, citing experts.

State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) advanced 3.52% week-over-week, while State Street Financial Sel Sec SPDR ETF (XLF) declined 1.83% amid renewed AI disruption fears.

Banks, insurers, and other related stocks that depend on consumer inertia came under pressure from the early popularity of Meta's Muse, an AI agent that executes multi-step tasks on a user's behalf.

Payment stocks slumped over disruption fears when a Muse checkout screen featured Meta Pay as an option, a report by Bloomberg showed.

Meta's Muse AI agent is reshaping sector rotation as risk appetite grows among investors, a separate Bloomberg report noted. On the other hand, XLF hit its lowest level since early July.

Among financial megacap stocks, Wells Fargo (WFC) led the decliners, shedding 3.66% from the prior week to close at $82.97.

The week saw the Wall Street giant announce the retirement of its chief risk officer, Derek Flowers. COO Scott Powell was named a successor.

"Derek played a pivotal role in strengthening our risk and control framework and fostering the strong risk culture that positions Wells Fargo for continued growth," CEO Charlie Scharf had said.

Morgan Stanley (MS) followed, with a 3.10% retreat to $196.31.

A Morgan Stanley employee is said to have accidentally leaked an internal document that had details on over 100 investment banking deals of the company in Asia and the EMEA region. The bank was working to contain the damage arising from the leak as regulators in India and China assessed the incident.

Citigroup (C) was the top advancer, adding 1.90% week-over-week to $134.28.

The week saw Citi sweetening the pot to lure new customers and persuade existing clients to bring more of their assets over to the bank by offering a higher savings rate under a new feature called Premium Boost.

Additionally, the company launched Citi Commerce Media, a platform that will use transaction-based data to help brands recognize emerging consumer needs, identify engagement opportunities, and measure campaigns' effectiveness.

Among largecap stocks, Pershing Square (PS) (+12.90% W/W to $56.16) was a notable winner. The week saw Bill Ackman's closed-end fund listed on the London Stock Exchange, Pershing Square Holdings (PSHZF), announce an up to $100M share repurchase program.

Ameriprise Financial (AMP) topped the losers. The stock lost 9.43% to close the week at $493.00 as the launch of Evergreen.ai, an AI-powered financial advice app, renewed AI disruption fears.

Allstate (ALL) followed with an 8.90% decrease to $227.60. Banks, insurers, and other related stocks that depend on consumer inertia had come under pressure from the early popularity of Meta's Muse, an AI agent that executes multi-step tasks on a user's behalf.

Lincoln International (LCLN) (-10.49% W/W to $23.37) led the midcap decliners amid AI disruption fears.

Figure Technology Solutions (FIGR) was the second largest loser, falling 10.12% from the previous week to $31.90. Bitcoin (BTC-USD) was hit after an economic report indicated hotter-than-expected business activity.

Miami International (MIAX) (-10.03% W/W to $34.90) was the next on the list. The company said on Thursday its full-service futures commission merchant, Dorman Trading, is now a clearing member of The Options Clearing Corporation.

Brighthouse Financial (BHF) (+6.59% W/W to $53.24) was a winner in the category after a report that Sixth Street is considering a renewed bid to buy the life insurer as a pending deal with Aquarian languished under regulatory review.

StablecoinX (USDE), a stablecoin infrastructure company, was a notable smallcap gainer, adding 69.28% week-over-week to $17.25. Orion180 Insurance (OIG) (-17.92% W/W to $9.57) was a major loser.

data.title: Notable analyst calls this week: Nike, Microsoft and CoreWeave among top picks
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) closed in the green on Friday, as further development around the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz continued.

Nasdaq (COMP:IND) rose over 1% for the week, while the Dow (DJI) lost nearly 1%. Wall Street had a slew of upgrades and downgrades from analysts. Here are some of the major calls for the week:

BofA downgrades Nike, says turnaround taking longer to materialize

Bank of America downgraded Nike (NKE) to Underperform from Neutral, saying the company’s turnaround is taking longer to materialize as weakness in its larger lifestyle categories overshadows product innovation.

Analyst Lorraine Hutchinson cut its price target to $30 from $47 and lowered its fiscal 2027 and 2028 EPS estimates by 11% and 12%, respectively, to $1.43 and $1.87. The firm now expects “negative sales growth through F27,” pushing the sales turnaround into fiscal 2028.

The brokerage said North American wholesale growth has not been matched by sell-through, with declines in classic styles and some new launches putting “forward order books at risk” as retailers become more cautious.

Microsoft upgraded as Stifel says tech giant is 'getting back on track'

Microsoft (MSFT) was upgraded to Buy from Hold at Stifel, as the investment firm said the tech giant is “getting back on track.”

“We are increasingly comfortable with the company's ability to sustain mid/upper teens revenue growth as open-weight model advancement has boosted management's LLM agnostic strategy (Azure & Copilot), COGS/OPEX operational efficiencies are supportive of stable operating margins and strong cash-flows should limit the company's need for outside financing,” Stifel analyst Brad Reback wrote.

Reback also increased his price target on Microsoft to $575 from $530 and added that he expects “accelerating” revenue growth in Azure.

CoreWeave on spotlight after JPM upgrade

CoreWeave (CRWV) was upgraded by J.P. Morgan to Overweight from Neutral, citing its “favorable” contracts that should boost revenue growth.

“We are upgrading CoreWeave to Overweight from Neutral, led by the favorable pricing backdrop for compute given the strong demand backdrop as well as the incremental willingness of the company to lean into short-term contracts at premium pricing, which drives our revenue and margin forecasts higher in contrast to a lackluster share price performance dictated by investor concerns around capital intensity,” analyst Samik Chatterjee wrote and upped his PT to $125 from $120.

Delving deeper, Chatterjee said the stronger pricing backdrop is due to a “robust demand environment,” which has strengthened throughout the year.

UBS downgrades PG&E as wildfire reform catalyst fades

UBS downgraded California utility company PG&E (PCG) to Neutral from Buy with a $14 price target, cut from $19, citing a growing risk of inaction on wildfire liability reform this year and the company’s decision to rescind its long-term earnings growth rate guidance alongside its strategic review announcement.

The brokerage lowered its long-term EPS growth rate forecast for PG&E (PCG) to 8.5% from 9% as he compounded the company's $2B capital expenditure deferral in 2027-30 and noted that tax loss selling pressure and interest rate risk make the stock incrementally less attractive.

Comcast downgraded by KeyBanc to Underweight

KeyBanC Capital Markets downgraded Comcast (CMCSA) to Underweight and cut its price target to $18, citing worsening broadband subscriber trends, pressure on cable profitability, and weaker theme-park attendance.

Analyst Brandon Nispel expects Comcast’s domestic broadband net losses to widen to 665,000 in 2027, below consensus for a 482,000 decline. The analyst said universal attendance weakened through August, with total attendance down 3% year-on-year and Epic Universe’s average daily attendance falling to about 13,000 from 16,000 in July.

Nispel also said it did not view Comcast’s NBCUniversal spin-off as a catalyst, citing deteriorating fundamentals and the loss of share-repurchase support.

Twilio (TWLO) was downgraded at HSBC as the investment firm said the hype from Meta Platforms (META) Muse artificial intelligence agent is adding volume but not conviction. The brokerage lowered rating to Reduce from Hold but kept its $211 PT on the stock.

Sandisk (SNDK) was in the spotlight as investment firm Rosenblatt Securities initiated coverage on the storage maker with a Buy rating and a $2,400 price target.

“New AI compute platforms are creating an opportunity to reposition NAND Flash (NAND) from a commodity storage medium to a more system-critical component of AI infrastructure. Historically, consumer, PC, and smartphone NAND demand was driven primarily by rising density and falling cost per bit,” analyst Kevin Cassidy wrote.
